title: Acto seguido: lo que ocurre inmediatamente después

sections.content: Acto seguido (right after, immediately following) marks that one event happened directly on the heels of another -- useful for narrating a quick sequence of events, like a rapid succession of leaders or decisions. It typically opens a sentence or clause. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Acto seguido, Roberto Eduardo Viola asumió la presidencia, pero permaneció en el cargo apenas nueve meses.
items.english: Right after, Roberto Eduardo Viola took office as president, but remained in the post barely nine months.

items.spanish: Galtieri asumió el poder; acto seguido, ordenó la invasión de las islas Malvinas.
items.english: Galtieri took power; right after, he ordered the invasion of the Falkland Islands.

items.spanish: Tras la derrota, Galtieri fue reemplazado, acto seguido, por Reynaldo Bignone.
items.english: After the defeat, Galtieri was replaced, immediately after, by Reynaldo Bignone.

items.spanish: El nuevo comandante asumió el cargo; acto seguido, comenzó a organizar la salida hacia un gobierno civil.
items.english: The new commander took office; right after, he began organizing the exit toward civilian government.

sections.content: Acto seguido is more compact and narrative than inmediatamente después -- it works especially well linking two short clauses in a quick sequence of historical events, one right after another.
